mechanism_narrative: A low and decreasing FEDFUNDS rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low and decreasing, but the S&P 500 shows negative returns over the next 20 days in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4%, but the S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which is positive for equity markets.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5%, but the S&P 500 shows negative returns over the next 5 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE indicate a tightening monetary policy, which can lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is rising and UNRATE is falling, but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity and supply chain health, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases, but the S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) and employment (PAYEMS) indicate strong consumer demand and economic growth, which is positive for equity markets.
failure_condition: If RSAFS and PAYEMS are rising, but the S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) may lead to inflation concerns, prompting tighter monetary policy and negative equity returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%, but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE) coupled with high FEDFUNDS may indicate stagflation, leading to negative equity returns as corporate earnings are squeezed.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is high and FEDFUNDS is high, but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days in more than 50% of cases.
